name: Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathologic and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma

criteria.description: Presence of spindle to epithelioid tumor cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in fascicles
Strong and diffuse expression of keratin (AE1/AE3) and FOSB positivity with variable CD31 and ERG expression
Detection of SERPINE1-FOSB gene fusion by molecular genetic testing
Multifocal lesions predominantly involving distal extremities soft tissue and bone

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic features plus immunohistochemical profile with molecular confirmation of SERPINE1-FOSB fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunophenotype, and molecular genetics due to overlap with other epithelioid vascular tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multifocal nodular soft tissue masses in distal extremities
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as multiple nodules or plaques on limbs
searchTerms: multiple soft tissue lumps in hands or feet
clustered soft tissue masses in fingers or toes

pathognomonic.notes: Localized tenderness and discomfort at lesion sites

common.symptomName: Involvement of underlying bone with lytic lesions
common.notes: Radiologic evidence of bone erosion or destruction
searchTerms: bone damage under soft tissue lesions

common.notes: Redness and mild inflammation of skin covering nodules
Lesions enlarge gradually over months to years
searchTerms: gradual increase in skin patch size

common.symptomName: Local edema adjacent to tumor nodules
common.notes: Swelling around affected soft tissue areas

occasional.notes: Rarely lesions may ulcerate due to surface ischemia

occasional.symptomName: Restricted joint mobility near lesion sites
occasional.notes: Functional impairment due to mass effect
Occasional enlargement of nearby lymph nodes

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

rare.symptomName: Pathologic fractures due to bone involvement
rare.notes: Fractures secondary to tumor-induced bone weakening
Occasional nerve impingement causing sensory changes
searchTerms: tingling or numbness due to nerve pressure

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: MRI showing multifocal soft tissue masses with heterogeneous enhancement
X-ray demonstrating lytic bone lesions adjacent to soft tissue nodules
CT scan for detection of pulmonary metastases
other: Histopathology revealing spindle to epithelioid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for keratin (AE1/AE3), FOSB, variable CD31 and ERG

distinguishingFeatures: Loss of INI1 expression on immunohistochemistry
Presence of WWTR1-CAMTA1 or YAP1-TFE3 gene fusions

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of soft tissue nodules
Development of ulceration or necrosis over lesions
Onset of respiratory symptoms suggesting metastasis
references: Hornick JL, Fletcher CD. Pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma: a distinctive, often multicentric tumor with indolent behavior. Am J Surg Pathol. 2011.
Errani C, Zhang L, Sung YS, et al. A novel SERPINE1-FOSB fusion gene results from t(7;19)(q22;q13) in pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma. Genes Chromosomes Cancer. 2014.
